diagnostic_evidence.quote: Recall $\Delta_{1}(1)=1$ and $\Delta_{\ell}(1)=0$ for $\ell\neq1$ because the Gauss--Hermite rule integrates constant functions exactly.
the roots of the univariate Hermite polynomial $H_{n}$ of degree $n$
Let $S_{\Lambda}$ be the corresponding sparse-grid quadrature based on the Gauss--Hermite rule.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims the lower bound is independent of the quadrature weights and that no choice of weights can improve the rate. What is proved (thm:GH-lower-bound-general, thm:lower-isotropic-Smolyak) is the lower bound for the single specific Smolyak rule S_Lambda built from the Gauss--Hermite rules. The annihilation S_Lambda(h_Lambda)=Q^uni_{lbar_1}(p_n)=0 uses two weight-dependent inputs: the telescoping reduction sum_l Delta_l(p_n)=Q^uni_{lbar_1}(p_n) together with Delta_l(1)=delta_{l,1} (each univariate rule exact for constants), and node vanishing only at the zeros of H_{n_{lbar_1}}, i.e. at the nodes of the single top-level rule. Because Gauss--Hermite rules at different levels are non-nested, a general re-weighting of the full sparse-grid node set is not annihilated by p_n(x_1): nodes whose first coordinate is a zero of some H_{n_j} with j<lbar_1 have p_n(x_1) nonzero and receive arbitrary weights. So the advertised weight-robustness scope exceeds what the argument establishes.

failure_location.quote: The lower bound is obtained by exploiting the structure of the Gauss--Hermite nodes and is independent of the quadrature weights; consequently, no modification of the weights can improve the rate $N^{-\alpha/2}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either narrow the claim to weight modifications preserving the Smolyak combination with univariate rules exact for constants (the case actually covered), or replace p_n by a bump function vanishing at the whole first-coordinate node set union_{l<=lbar_1}{zeros of H_{n_l}} and re-estimate its H^alpha_rho norm using the near-uniform bulk spacing of the finest level, which yields the same N^{-alpha/2}-type bound for arbitrary weights.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised claim that no modification of the weights can improve the rate N^{-alpha/2} is unsupported as written; the formal lower bounds for the specific sparse-grid rule S_Lambda remain valid.
issues.title: Weight-robustness of the sparse-grid lower bound is claimed but not proved
issues.why_classification: No theorem, rate or method is lost, but closing the gap needs either a limited weakening of an advertised scope claim or a modified fooling function together with a new node-distribution estimate (the quasi-uniformity of Hermite zeros is not supplied in the source); this exceeds a routine local edit.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts that n_{L-d+1} >= e^{d-1} implies (ln n_{L-d+1})^{d-1} <= n_{L-d+1}, i.e. (d-1) ln ln n <= ln n. This is false for d >= 4: e.g. d=4, n=21 satisfies ln n > 3 = d-1 but (ln 21)^3 approx 28.2 > 21. Consequently the derived estimate ln N \lesssim_d 2 ln n_{L-d+1} (the constant 2 is also too small in this regime) is unproved, and the final comparison n^{-alpha/2} \gtrsim_d N^{-alpha/2}(ln N)^{alpha(d-1)/2} does not follow as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false implication by the valid bound ln N <= C_d ln n_{L-d+1} (which does hold for n_{L-d+1} >= e^{d-1}, since (d-1)ln u/u is bounded for u >= d-1) and absorb the factor C_d^{alpha(d-1)/2} into c_{alpha,d}; alternatively strengthen the hypothesis to n_{L-d+1} >= (d-1)^{d-1}-type. Statement and rate unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The last step of the proof of thm:lower-isotropic-Smolyak is invalid, and thm:added-1 (isotropic part), which explicitly follows the same arguments, inherits the gap. The stated bounds themselves are not lost.
issues.title: Isotropic lower bound: (ln n)^{d-1} <= n does not follow from ln n >= d-1
issues.why_classification: A one-line change of constants repairs the inference; the hypothesis, conclusion, rate and the logarithmic factor all survive unchanged, since the theorem's constant is already allowed to depend on d.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\mathscr{I}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{uni}}$ is the polynomial interpolation operator using the zeros of $H_{n_{\ell}+1}$.
the roots of the univariate Hermite polynomial $H_{n}$ of degree $n$

issues.failure_explanation: In the proof, p_n is built on the zeros of H_n with n = n_{lbar_1}, the number of nodes of the Gauss--Hermite rule Q^uni_{lbar_1} (so that Q^uni_{lbar_1}(p_n)=0), whereas I^uni_{lbar_1} is defined to interpolate at the zeros of H_{n_{lbar_1}+1}. The displayed identity |int p_n rho - Q^uni_{lbar_1}(p_n)| = |int [p_n - I^uni_{lbar_1}(p_n)] rho| ('since I is interpolatory') requires Q^uni_{lbar_1} to be the interpolatory quadrature of I^uni_{lbar_1}, i.e. identical nodes. With the two different node sets the equality is false (int I^uni_{lbar_1}(p_n) rho is the (n+1)-point interpolatory rule at the zeros of H_{n+1} applied to p_n, not Q^uni_{lbar_1}(p_n)=0), so the reduction of the L1 approximation error to the known univariate integration lower bound does not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the definitions and take as fooling function p_{n_{lbar_1}+1} (bumps on the zeros of H_{n_{lbar_1}+1}, i.e. the interpolation nodes), so that I_Lambda(h)=0 and ||h-I_Lambda h||_{L1} = ||p_{n+1}||_{L1} >= int p_{n+1} rho, with the same one-dimensional estimate and n_{lbar_1}+1 <= N; or redefine I^uni_l to interpolate at the zeros of H_{n_l}, which makes the displayed identity valid.
issues.overall_effect: Both lower bounds in thm:added-1 (general downward-closed index set and isotropic index set) are left unproved by the given argument.
issues.title: Sparse-grid interpolation lower bound: quadrature and interpolation use different node sets
issues.why_classification: Both repairs are local and reuse the existing one-dimensional estimate; both statements and their rates N^{-alpha/2} and N^{-alpha/2}(ln N)^{alpha(d-1)/2} are preserved with no new lemma or replacement argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The value $b$ controls the truncation error

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated parameter one has b^2 = (alpha/2) ln N, so the part of the error outside the box [-b,b]^d is far too large for (eq:aff-lattice-error). Concrete counterexample: take f(x) = psi(x_1) with psi a fixed smooth bump supported in [b+1,b+2] and equal to 1 in its middle. Every evaluation point lies in [-b,b]^d, so Q_N(f)=0 exactly, while I(f) \asymp_alpha rho_1(b+3/2) and ||f||_{H^alpha_rho}^2 \asymp_alpha rho_1(b+3/2), giving |I(f)-Q_N(f)|/||f|| \asymp_alpha e^{-(b+3/2)^2/4} \gtrsim N^{-alpha/4}. This contradicts the claimed upper bound C N^{-alpha}(ln N)^{(3 alpha d)/2 + d/4}, since N^{-alpha/4}/(N^{-alpha}(ln N)^K) -> infinity. The proof never bounds this truncation term; its own decay estimate only yields int_{outside}|f rho| <= C_eps ||f|| e^{-eps b^2/2} = C_eps ||f|| N^{-eps alpha/4} for eps in (0,1/2), which is never O(N^{-alpha}). The companion result prop:added-2 uses the larger radius b = 2 sqrt(alpha ln N), at which scale the truncation is consistent with an N^{-alpha} rate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Enlarge the truncation radius to b = c sqrt(alpha ln N) with c > 2 (e.g. the b = 2 sqrt(alpha ln N) used in prop:added-2) and add the truncation estimate int_{R^d minus box}|f rho| <= C_eps ||f|| e^{-eps b^2/2} = O(N^{-alpha}) using the decay bound already proved in the same proof. Since b \asymp sqrt(ln N) as before, the N^{-alpha} rate and the stated logarithmic power are unchanged in form.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:lattice-affin is false as stated, so the first case ('Rank-1 lattice rule with affine map') of thm:qmc-summary, and with it the abstract's and introduction's claim that all four QMC constructions attain the optimal polynomial rate N^{-alpha} up to logarithms, are unreliable for that construction.
issues.title: Affinely-mapped lattice rule: truncation radius too small, claimed rate false
issues.why_classification: The guarantee, method and rate class survive, but the repair is a genuine re-selection of the truncation parameter (balancing truncation against the QMC error) plus a missing contained estimate, rather than a single forced correction; the parameter must be re-derived before the advertised bound can stand.
